statement: If x and y are in direct proportion then y = kx, so the constant is k = y/x for nonzero x.
A linear equation of the form ax = b has solution x = b/a, defined when a ≠ 0.
The y-intercept of y = ax² + bx + c is c.
The axis of symmetry of y = ax² + bx + c is x = −b/2a.
If y is inversely proportional to x then y = k/x, so the constant is k = xy.
The vertical asymptote of y = a/(x−b) is x = b.
The horizontal asymptote of y = a/(x−b) + d is y = d.
(x−a)(x−b) = x² − (a+b)x + ab.
(x−a) is a factor of polynomial p(x) if and only if p(a) = 0.
If (x−a) is a factor of a cubic p(x), then p(x) = (x−a)q(x) where q(x) is a quadratic polynomial.
f(a) is the value of f(x) obtained by substituting x = a into the rule for f.
Under a vertical translation of a units, a point with y-coordinate y maps to y + a.
Under a horizontal translation of h units, a point with x-coordinate x maps to x + h.
Under a vertical dilation by factor c, a point with y-coordinate y maps to cy.
Under the horizontal dilation taking y = f(x) to y = f(kx), a point with x-coordinate x maps to x/k.
For t >= 0, sqrt(t) denotes the non-negative square root of t; it is the unique s >= 0 with s^2 = t.
If y = kx and k is known, the value at x is kx.
(x-a)(x-b)(x-c) expands to x^3 - (a+b+c)x^2 + (ab+bc+ca)x - abc.
Translating y = p(x) by a adds a to the constant term.
Dilating y = p(x) vertically by c multiplies every coefficient by c.
The value of y = a/(x-b) + d at a given x, defined when x != b.
For y = ax^2 + bx + c with axis x = p, b = -2ap.
If y = k/x and k is known, the value at x is k/x.
